entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 4 Ho 4:1-19 . Henceforth the Prophet Speaks Plainly and without Symbol, in Terse, Sententious Propositions. In this chapter he reproves the people and priests for their sins in the interregnum which followed Jeroboam's death; hence there is no mention of the king or his family; and in Ho 4:2 bloodshed and other evils usual in a civil war are specified. 1. Israel-- the ten tribes. controversy-- judicial ground of complaint ( Is 1:18 ; Jr 25:31 ; Mi 6:2 ). no ... knowledge of God-- exhibited in practice ( Jr 22:16 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12284"/><div sID="gen22378" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12284"/><hi type="bold">8. eat ... sin of my people--</hi>that is, the sin offerings (<reference osisRef="Lev.6.26">Le 6:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.10.17">10:17</reference>). The special reference here is to the licentious orgies connected with the Syrian worship, which lured Israel away from the pure worship of God (<reference osisRef="Isa.28.1">Is 28:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.28.7">7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.4.1">Am 4:1</reference>).<div eID="gen22384" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22385" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">take away the heart--</hi>that is, the understanding; make men blind to their own true good (<reference osisRef="Eccl.7.7">Ec 7:7</reference>). <div eID="gen22385" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12288"/><div sID="gen22386" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12288"/>12. entries.content_plain: 12. Instances of their understanding ("heart") being "taken away." stocks-- wooden idols ( Jr 2:27 ; Ha 2:19 ). staff-- alluding to divination by rods (see on Eze 21:21 , 22 ). The diviner, says Rosenmuller, threw a rod from him, which was stripped of its bark on one side, not on the other: if the bare side turned uppermost, it was a good omen; if the side with the bark, it was a bad omen. The Arabs used two rods, the one marked God bids, the other, God forbids; whichever came out first, in drawing them out of a case, gave the omen for, or against, an undertaking. declareth-- that is, is consulted to inform them of future events. spirit of whoredoms-- a general disposition on the part of all towards idolatry ( Ho 5:4 ). err-- go astray from the true God. from under their God-- They have gone away from God under whom they were, as a wife is under the dominion of her husband.

I will not punish ... daughters--</hi>I will visit with the heaviest punishments "not" the unchaste "daughters and spouses," but the fathers and husbands; for it is these who "themselves" have set the bad example, so that as compared with the punishment of the latter, that of the former shall seem as nothing [Munster].<div eID="gen22397" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22398" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">separated with whores--</hi>withdrawn from the assembly of worshippers to some receptacle of impurity for carnal connection with whores.<div eID="gen22398" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22399" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sacrifice with harlots--</hi>They commit lewdness with women who devote their persons to be violated in honor of Astarte. Compare <reference osisRef="Num.25.1-Num.25.3">Nu 25:1-3</reference>; and the prohibition, <reference osisRef="Deut.23.18">De 23:18</reference>.<div eID="gen22399" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22400" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">not understand--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.44.18">Is 44:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.45.20">45:20</reference>).<div eID="gen22400" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22401" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall fall--</hi>shall be cast down. <div eID="gen22401" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 14. I will not punish ... daughters-- I will visit with the heaviest punishments "not" the unchaste "daughters and spouses," but the fathers and husbands; for it is these who "themselves" have set the bad example, so that as compared with the punishment of the latter, that of the former shall seem as nothing [Munster]. separated with whores-- withdrawn from the assembly of worshippers to some receptacle of impurity for carnal connection with whores. sacrifice with harlots-- They commit lewdness with women who devote their persons to be violated in honor of Astarte. (So the Hebrew for "harlots" means, as distinguished from "whores"). Compare Nu 25:1-3 ; and the prohibition, De 23:18 . not understand-- ( Is 44:18 ; 45:20 ). shall fall-- shall be cast down.
entries.reader_content_plain: 14. I will not punish ... daughters-- I will visit with the heaviest punishments "not" the unchaste "daughters and spouses," but the fathers and husbands; for it is these who "themselves" have set the bad example, so that as compared with the punishment of the latter, that of the former shall seem as nothing [Munster]. separated with whores-- withdrawn from the assembly of worshippers to some receptacle of impurity for carnal connection with whores. sacrifice with harlots-- They commit lewdness with women who devote their persons to be violated in honor of Astarte. (So the Hebrew for "harlots" means, as distinguished from "whores"). Compare Nu 25:1-3 ; and the prohibition, De 23:18 . not understand-- ( Is 44:18 ; 45:20 ). shall fall-- shall be cast down.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12291"/><div sID="gen22402" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12291"/>15. Though Israel's ten tribes indulge in spiritual harlotry, at least thou, Judah, who hast the legal priesthood, and the temple rites, and Jerusalem, do not follow her bad example.<div eID="gen22402" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22403" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Gilgal--</hi>situated between Jordan and Jericho on the confines of Samaria; once a holy place to Jehovah (<reference osisRef="Josh.5.10-Josh.5.15">Jos 5:10-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.10.8">1Sa 10:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.15.21">15:21</reference>); afterwards desecrated by idol-worship (<reference osisRef="Hos.9.15">Ho 9:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.12.11">12:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.4.4">Am 4:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.5.5">5:5</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Judg.3.19">Jud 3:19</reference>, Margin).<div eID="gen22403" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22404" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Beth-aven--</hi>that is, "house of vanity" or idols: a name substituted in contempt for Beth-el, "the house of God"; once sacred to Jehovah (<reference osisRef="Gen.28.17">Ge 28:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.28.19">19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gen.35.7">35:7</reference>), but made by Jeroboam the seat of the worship of the calves (1Ki 12:28-33; 13:1; <reference osisRef="Jer.48.13">Jr 48:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.3.14">Am 3:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.7.13">7:13</reference>). "Go up" refers to the fact that Beth-el was on a hill (<reference osisRef="Josh.16.1">Jos 16:1</reference>).<div eID="gen22404" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22405" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">nor swear, The Lord liveth--</hi>This formula of oath was appointed by God Himself (<reference osisRef="Deut.6.13">De 6:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.10.20">10:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.4.2">Jr 4:2</reference>). It is therefore here forbidden not absolutely, but in conjunction with idolatry and falsehood (<reference osisRef="Isa.48.1">Is 48:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.20.39">Eze 20:39</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zeph.1.5">Zep 1:5</reference>). <div eID="gen22405" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12292"/><div sID="gen22406" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12292"/><hi type="bold">16. backsliding--</hi>Translate, "Israel is refractory, as a refractory heifer," namely, one that throws the yoke off her neck. Israel had represented God under the form of "calves" (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.12.28">1Ki 12:28</reference>); but it is she herself who is one.<div eID="gen22406" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22407" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">lamb in a large place--</hi>not in a good sense, as in <reference osisRef="Isa.30.23">Is 30:23</reference>. Here there is irony: lambs like a large pasture; but it is not so safe for them as a small one, duly fenced from wild beasts. God will "feed" them, but it shall be with the "rod" (<reference osisRef="Mic.7.14">Mi 7:14</reference>). It shall be no longer in the narrow territory of Israel, but "in a large place," namely, they shall be scattered in exile over the wide realm of Assyria, a prey to their foes; as lambs, which are timid, gregarious, and not solitary, are a prey when scattered asunder to wild beasts. <div eID="gen22407" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12294"/><div sID="gen22412" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12294"/><hi type="bold">18. Their drink is sour--</hi>metaphor for utter degeneracy of principle (<reference osisRef="Isa.1.22">Is 1:22</reference>). Or, unbridled licentiousness; not mere ordinary sin, but as abandoned as drunkards who vomit and smell sour with wine potations [Calvin]. Maurer not so well translates, "When their drinking is over, they commit whoredoms," namely, in honor of Astarte (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.13">Ho 4:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.14">14</reference>).<div eID="gen22412" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22413" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">her rulers--</hi>Israel's; literally, "shields" (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.47.9">Psa 47:9</reference>).<div eID="gen22413" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22414" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">with shame ... love, Give ye--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Prov.30.15">Pr 30:15</reference>). No remedy could be effectual against their corruptions since the very rulers sold justice for gifts [Calvin]. Maurer translates, "The rulers are marvelously enamored of shame." English Version is better. <div eID="gen22414" type="x-p"/>
